findings.title: website_name bypasses the anonymous TL0 profile redaction
findings.body: `website` is explicitly listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so anonymous viewers of a TL0 user do not receive it, but the newly added `website_name` attribute is not. As a result, those responses now expose the host portion of a profile website (for example an employer or personal site) despite the website field being intentionally hidden. Add `website_name` to the untrusted attributes/redaction logic and add coverage to the anonymous-TL0 serializer test.

findings.title: The website_name inclusion predicate is named incorrectly and is ignored
findings.body: Serializer attribute predicates in this class use the `include_<attribute>?` form (for example `include_email?`). `include_website_name` lacks the question mark, so the serializer will not use it to decide whether to emit the attribute. Consequently `website_name` is emitted by default even for profiles without a website or with an unparsable URL, producing an unintended `null` field rather than being omitted as this method attempts to specify. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (while ensuring the redaction predicate is also preserved).

findings.title: Same-domain detection is case-sensitive for DNS hostnames
findings.body: `URI(...).host` preserves hostname casing, while DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. A valid profile URL such as `http://EXAMPLE.COM/user` on an `example.com` instance fails the equality and suffix comparisons and is displayed as only `EXAMPLE.COM`, rather than including `/user` as required for the same domain. Normalize both parsed and instance hostnames (for example, `downcase` and ideally remove a trailing DNS dot) before comparing them.
